blogs.title: Goodbye Tokens, Hello Patches: How the Byte Latent Transformer Changes AI Efficiency
blogs.description: An accessible breakdown of the Byte Latent Transformer (BLT), explaining how it replaces the traditional 'tokenization' step with dynamic 'patches.' This post explores how grouping raw bytes based on complexity allows AI models to save up to 50% of their computational power during inference while matching the performance of giants like Llama 3.

blogs.title: Why AI Struggles with Typos (and How Reading Raw Bytes Fixes It)
blogs.description: A deep dive into the robustness advantages of byte-level models. We explain why standard AI models often fail when faced with scrambled text, weird capitalization, or rare languages, and how BLT's ability to process raw characters gives it a superpower for understanding noise and handling low-resource languages.

blogs.title: The New Scaling Law: How to Make Bigger Models Without Spending More Money
blogs.description: A strategic look at the future of Large Language Model scaling. This post explains the counter-intuitive finding that by making 'patches' larger (grouping more bytes together), we can actually build bigger, smarter models within the same fixed budget, unlocking a new dimension of growth that token-based models cannot achieve.

blogs.title: Smart Computing: How AI Decides When to Think Hard and When to Skim
blogs.description: An explanation of the 'Entropy Patching' mechanism in BLT. Using simple analogies, we describe how the model dynamically allocates its brainpower—spending less compute on predictable text (like common words) and reserving heavy processing for complex, high-uncertainty sections, mimicking human reading efficiency.
